title: Functions and Graphs
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Functions and Graphs. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Function rule

A function assigns exactly one output to each permitted input. The domain is the allowed input set and the range is the resulting output set. In (f(\(x\))), the symbol names the output; it is not multiplication.

Domain restrictions

For real-valued expressions, a denominator cannot be zero and the radicand of an even root must be nonnegative. For (\(f(x)=1/(x-2)\)), exclude (\(x=2\)); for (\(g(x)=\sqrt{x-3}\)), require (\(x \ge 3\)).

Graphs and transformations

The graph consists of points ((x,f(\(x\)))). A vertical line intersects a function's graph at most once. The x-intercepts solve (\(f(x)=0\)); the y-intercept is (\(f(0)\)) when defined. Replacing (\(x\)) by (x-h) shifts a graph right by (\(h\)); adding (\(k\)) shifts it upward by (\(k\)).

Worked example: For (\(f(x)=x^2-4x+3\)), factor as (\((x-1)(x-3)\)); the x-intercepts are 1 and 3, while the y-intercept is (\(f(0)=3\)).

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• For (\(f(a+h)\)), substitute the entire expression (\(a+h\)) wherever (\(x\)) appears.
  • Check denominator and root restrictions before stating a domain.
  • Use intercepts and symmetry to sketch simple polynomial graphs.
  • A graph may pass the vertical-line test without being one-to-one.
  • For composition, evaluate the inside function first.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• For (\(f(x)=mx+c\)), slope is (\(m\)) and y-intercept is (\(c\)).
  • For (\(f(x)=x^2\)), outputs are nonnegative and the graph is symmetric about the y-axis.
  • Horizontal-line test is a test for one-to-one behavior, not for being a function.
  • Inverse functions swap input and output and require one-to-one restriction.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    If (\(f(x)=2x^2+1\)), what is (\(f(-2)\))?

    1. (\(5\))
    2. (\(7\))
    3. (\(9\))
    4. (\(-7\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(9\))

    Substitute (\(-2\)): (\(f(-2)=2(-2)^2+1=2\cdot4+1=9\)).

  2. Core:

    What is the real domain of (\(g(x)=\sqrt{x-5}\))?

    1. (\(x<5\))
    2. (\(x\le5\))
    3. (\(x>5\))
    4. (\(x\ge5\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(x\ge5\))

    The radicand must be nonnegative: (\(x-5\ge0\)), so (\(x\ge5\)).

  3. Foundation:

    If (\(f(x)=3x-2\)), find (\(f(5)\)).

    1. (\(11\))
    2. (\(13\))
    3. (\(15\))
    4. (\(17\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(13\))

    Substitute 5: (\(f(5)=3(5)-2=13\)).

  4. Standard:

    What is the real domain of (\(g(x)=1/(x^2-9)\))?

    1. All real x
    2. (\(x eq 3 only\))
    3. (\(x eq -3 only\))
    4. (\(x eq -3 and x eq 3\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(x eq -3 and x eq 3\))

    The denominator factors as (\((x-3)(x+3)\)); exclude both values (\(-3\)) and 3.

  5. Challenge:

    For (\(h(x)=x^2+2x\)), what is the minimum value over the real numbers?

    1. (\(-2\))
    2. (\(-1\))
    3. (\(0\))
    4. (\(1\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(-1\))

    Complete the square: (\(x^2+2x=(x+1)^2-1\)). Since a square is at least zero, the minimum is (\(-1\)).
